candidates.title: Send daily alerts for new target-company jobs

demandEvidence.chore: Track target companies' career pages and send an alert when a new job appears.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Sharing a simple pattern I use for tracking hiring at target companies. Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack.

experimentPlan.output: A daily review list of newly found jobs from a small set of operator-selected target companies, with a short proposed match note.
inputs: Operator-supplied role keywords and location preferences
Public job listing title, location and URL
experimentPlan.trigger: A scheduled daily check of the operator's selected public career pages.
steps: Read the operator's approved target-company list.
Check public career pages for new listings using an authorized retrieval method.
Compare listing URLs with the prior run's saved list.
Draft a brief match note from operator-supplied role preferences.
Send only new listing links and notes to a private review channel.
Ask the operator to verify relevance and access permission before acting.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Given a small fixture of previously seen and new listings, confirm that only new URLs appear and each match note cites the supplied preference it used.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies target companies and preferences, confirms retrieval is permitted, reviews every listing and note, and decides whether to apply or contact anyone.
unverified: Generalizing the author's described workflow to other career sites
Whether the proposed match notes are useful or accurate
Permission and stability of each career site's public access
No software execution or student deployment is established by this draft

ease.reason: The retained workflow describes a daily trigger, new-item check and Slack alert; a test is plausible, but the source does not show unusually easy setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: recruiting consultancies may pay for monitoring; the author describes personal tracking and shows no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: The described daily flow supports a narrow test; broader site coverage and useful match notes remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The described repeated run returns new listings, while access, relevance and next actions still require a person.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe one author’s target-company tracking loop and alert fields; outside demand and matching usefulness are not established.

candidates.reason: Retained the proposed narrow daily alert experiment and its source-supported workflow. The repaired ratings are 6, 4, 6, 6 and 5 (mean 5.4), below the threshold.

candidates.title: Prepare resume fields for repeated applications

demandEvidence.chore: Repeatedly enter resume information into company-specific hiring forms.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable map from operator-provided resume text to fields in one sample application form.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a mapping run after supplying a resume and a sample form's field labels.
steps: Extract candidate facts from the supplied fictional resume text.
Map each fact to a matching supplied form label.
Leave unsupported or ambiguous fields blank.
Show the proposed values beside their source text.
Have a person verify every value and enter it manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed fictional resume and sample form, verify that every populated field is supported by a matching source phrase and ambiguous fields remain blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies the text, checks sensitive details, verifies every mapping, and manually submits any real application.
unverified: Company-specific form layouts and fields
Reliable field mapping beyond a small fixed example
Any browser entry or application submission
Willingness of job seekers to pay

ease.reason: The supplied Information Extractor documentation supports structured extraction from text, but does not document form filling or field matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers may pay to reduce repeated form entry; this single post shows a chore, not purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can prepare values for supplied labels; the extractor supports structured text output, while company forms and live entry remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Extraction can be tested on supplied text, but no field-mapping or browser capability is documented and a person must verify and submit each form.

evidence.reason: The post states a daily two-hour resume-entry chore for forms tailored to one or two companies; frequency beyond this account and buyer demand are unknown.

candidates.reason: Assessed a bounded extraction-and-review experiment; the documented extraction reference does not support form mapping or submission, and the provisional mean is below six.

candidates.title: Use an already received image in a reply assistant

demandEvidence.chore: Pass an already received customer image together with the message to an assistant instead of asking the customer to resend it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Even though the image has already been received and downloaded, the AI agent asks the customer to send the image again.

experimentPlan.output: A draft response that uses a supplied message and its associated sample image when both are present.
inputs: A manually paired message and image record
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test with a sample customer message and its attached image.
steps: Represent the message and image as one test record.
Check that the record includes both text and image fields.
Ask a model to describe only visible product attributes.
Draft a response that references those attributes cautiously.
Flag missing or uncertain image details for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For paired and image-missing fixtures, confirm the paired case uses the supplied image and the missing case asks for clarification without inventing product details.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies test media, checks image handling and every draft, and approves any customer-facing response.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents message-image pairing
Vision accuracy and platform image access
Live Messenger integration and privacy requirements
Whether the proposed service has paying customers

ease.reason: The post clearly describes the routing problem, but no supplied implementation reference documents combining image and text inputs.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay to reduce repeated image requests; the post shows a troubleshooting need, not purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fixture test is bounded, but image access, pairing and model accuracy are unsupported by supplied references.

autonomy.reason: A proposed paired-input draft loop is repeatable, but no supplied source supports its integration and a person must check every response.

evidence.reason: The retained original-post span states the image-resend failure and desired shared input; it gives no implementation or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete troubleshooting chore assessed with a synthetic paired-input experiment; absent integration support keeps the provisional mean below six.

candidates.title: Prevent booking conflicts in salon requests

demandEvidence.chore: Check incoming salon booking requests against working hours, staff availability and existing appointments before confirmation.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Every booking request checks salon working hours, master availability, and existing appointments in PostgreSQL at the SQL level before confirmation.

experimentPlan.output: A draft booking decision showing whether a fictional request conflicts with supplied salon hours, staff slots or appointments.
inputs: Fictional booking request with date and time
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one fictional booking request for a test run.
steps: Parse the requested date and time from the supplied fixture.
Compare it with the supplied working hours.
Check the selected staff member's fictional availability.
Check the fixture for an existing appointment in the requested slot.
Return a conflict explanation or a draft confirmation for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run fixtures for outside-hours, unavailable-staff, occupied-slot and clear-slot cases; verify each result matches the supplied deterministic rules.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and verifies test rules and records, reviews every decision, and confirms any real appointment.
unverified: The post's detailed architecture is absent from the retained task span
No supplied implementation reference independently supports execution
Real calendar access, concurrency handling and deployment
Payment interest from salon operators

ease.reason: The post's retained spans describe a proposed architecture, but no supplied implementation reference supports a student build.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: salons may pay for fewer booking conflicts; the maker's architecture post does not establish a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A fictional slot-check prototype is scoped for four weeks, but live calendar access and reliable concurrent booking are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed checks are repeatable, but no implementation capability is supplied here and a person must confirm real bookings.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe salon booking requests, atomic slot validation and a database architecture; they do not establish external demand.

candidates.reason: The retained spans describe a working architecture and bounded booking checks, but no separate implementation reference or outside buyer evidence is supplied; below threshold.

candidates.title: Monitor vulnerabilities on a Mac

demandEvidence.chore: Monitor new Mac vulnerabilities and identify what needs fixing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Built an open source tool that monitors new vulnerabilities every 15 mins and lets you or your agent know on what to fix.

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed daily list of vulnerability notices mapped to an operator-supplied inventory of fictional Mac software.
inputs: A small public vulnerability notice sample
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test after supplying the fictional inventory and notice sample.
steps: Normalize software names and versions in the fixture.
Compare fixture entries with supplied notices.
Flag possible matches with the matching text shown.
Draft a plain-language review note without prescribing remediation.
Have a qualified operator verify each match and decide any action.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed fixture with known matching and nonmatching versions, check that every flag cites the matched name and version and no remediation is issued automatically.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified person verifies notices, applicability and any remediation; the prototype does not scan devices or change software.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports vulnerability retrieval or matching
Accuracy and completeness of public notices
The author describes a tool, not demand from independent buyers
Security advice and remediation require qualified review

ease.reason: The post describes an existing tool but no supplied reference supports vulnerability feeds, version matching or a safe student prototype.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small IT consultancies might pay for vulnerability monitoring; this maker post establishes no buyer interest or payment.

feasibility.reason: A fictional comparison is possible, but useful matching and security conclusions are unsupported and need qualified review.

autonomy.reason: The safe version only drafts flags for review; no retrieval or validation capability is supported and remediation must remain human-led.

evidence.reason: The post says its author's tool monitors vulnerabilities every 15 minutes, but gives no independent user need or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Scored a narrow fictional matching experiment, but the source is a maker's product description and supplied evidence does not support safe monitoring or an independent buyer need.
